title: CLIO engineering walkthrough
takeaway: CLIO can carry an engineering request through cluster execution into results the researcher can explore and a studio for individual trials.
organization: Two related chapters: explore the design space with E4, then inspect the E5 studio. They are sibling sessions, not a single continuous run.
chronology: E5 was recorded earlier than E4. Chapter order is editorial. Switch through the native session context; never fabricate an E4 follow-up prompt that supposedly created E5.
subject: CLIO's work and the researcher's decisions. Explain only enough mechanics to understand the interaction.

delivery.master: 1920x1080, 60 fps, silent for the live presenter
delivery.review: Same film with visible burned captions below the full UI; retain the clean master
delivery.captions: Editable timed presenter draft, SRT/VTT, later real audio alignment using the existing ElevenLabs response importer
delivery.publication: Local deliverables only. No commit, push, YouTube upload or external message is part of planning.

e4.frameMeaning: Frames 0-11 are different cases, all at iteration 50. They are not optimization time steps.

lifecycle.T002-T008: failed attempts retained in the source

nativeChecks.evidence: Saved GLB renders through pinned production DashboardView and ArchiveTransport on port 3365.
Dragging one saved viewport rotates its peers.
Changing 0.50 to 0.35 updates the displayed geometry.
Clicking c05 updates the selected view and the file table to E4/results/c05/.
Geometry, setup and results render; density views, stress view and convergence chart load.
Eleven frames and /res/iter exist, but no iteration slider is exposed in the saved dashboard.
The source explicitly says routing was not demonstrated; lifecycle actions were run through tools/lifecycle.py. Exported interactions are empty.
All 36 stale running tool records are reconciled only against their matching semantic tool.call.completed events; source exports remain unchanged.

shots.title: The engineering request
shots.chat: Type a faithful excerpt of the real request to vary volume fraction and filter radius; retain the 12-case matrix.
shots.canvas: Keep the conversation dominant. No result geometry before its source creation.
shots.interaction: Submit the request with one measured, brisk pointer move.
shots.payoff: A recognizable CLIO request starts the work.
shots.caption: Explore the design space
shots.presenterCue: The researcher wants to compare twelve combinations of material budget and filter radius while keeping the rest of the problem fixed.

shots.title: CLIO reads the constraints and plans the work
shots.source: e4.requestId and following recorded public replies
shots.chat: Show relevant connected-data reads, short tool accumulation and public planning text. Include the recorded initial-density decision before submission.
shots.canvas: Use native tool detail if it can be pinned; otherwise retain the ordinary expanded tool row.
shots.interaction: Expand one useful input or plan detail, then compact it.
shots.payoff: The request becomes a concrete run matrix and execution plan.
shots.caption: Twelve cases under one specification
shots.presenterCue: CLIO checks the inputs, preserves the locked settings, and lays out the run matrix and storage plan before launching compute.

shots.title: Launch and monitor the sweep
shots.source: e4.calls.launchArray, call_bb2c24f185ff, captured queue/completion checks and the saved case-runtime table
shots.chat: Replay the actual array submission, background watcher launch and queue check. Hold the source during a short Later transition, then show collection and completion.
shots.canvas: Keep the ordinary conversation. No invented scheduler grid, interpolated elapsed clock or inferred per-case start times.
shots.interaction: Read the watcher launch and queue update before the editorial time cut.
shots.payoff: CLIO carries out and checks the cluster work.
shots.caption: Each case took 10–19 minutes
shots.presenterCue: The twelve cases run as a Slurm array. CLIO monitors execution and collects the summaries and final designs.

shots.title: Results become an interactive view
shots.chat: Show the relevant public explanation, registration and successful widget/dashboard creation before the interface appears.
shots.canvas: Open the native sweep dashboard only after its source boundary.
shots.interaction: Open the generated view through its actual native artifact/widget entry.
shots.payoff: The dashboard is visibly produced by the work in the chat.
shots.caption: Inspect the results
shots.presenterCue: The mesh data and result tables are registered and assembled into a dashboard. Each viewport represents one completed case.

shots.title: Explore the twelve designs
shots.chat: Freeze the complete source clock for this inspection; preserve the conversation for the return.
shots.canvas: Use native canvas expansion and a readable grid. Keep parameter labels visible; do not shrink an entire long dashboard into one frame.
shots.interaction: Make one short synchronized orbit, ending in a clear three-quarter view. Move the density threshold from 0.50 to 0.35, inspect the geometry change, then restore 0.50.
shots.payoff: The viewer sees actual differences and can distinguish a display threshold from a new solver run.
shots.caption: Compare the designs
shots.presenterCue: All twelve views share a camera. The density threshold changes which material is displayed; it does not rerun optimization or change the recorded performance numbers.

shots.title: A design stays linked to its evidence
shots.source: e4 cases.csv, case_files.csv and selected mesh frame 4
shots.chat: Keep the source paused while the researcher inspects a result, then restore the conversation.
shots.canvas: Reflow the case table, selected viewport and relevant file rows into a readable native canvas.
shots.interaction: Select c05, inspect its linked design and files, compare c10, then return to c05 before restoring the chat.
shots.payoff: The shape is connected to settings, numbers and source files.
shots.caption: Select a case
shots.presenterCue: Selecting a case updates the design and its evidence together. This is c05: volume fraction 0.15 and filter radius 0.15.

shots.title: Bring the completed branches together
shots.chat: Replay the actual comparison request, then the recorded report publication. Source order is preserved.
shots.canvas: Keep the previous completed sweep in context until the next report is published.
shots.interaction: The next report opens after successful publication.
shots.payoff: CLIO brings related work into a usable comparison.
shots.caption: Inspect the same case in detail
shots.presenterCue: The follow-up work adds solver comparisons and smoothed representations. We inspect one corresponding case while retaining the links to the underlying studies.

shots.title: Inspect a comparison without touring every report
shots.chat: Retain the actual request for the combined report and its successful publication; omit repetitive report-building boilerplate.
shots.canvas: One Morphorm case before and after smoothing, using the native saved viewports and identical camera.
shots.interaction: Inspect c05 with one short synchronized orbit.
shots.payoff: CLIO brings related work into a usable comparison.
shots.caption: Inspect the same case in detail
shots.presenterCue: The same Morphorm result can be inspected as a density threshold and a smoothed surface. No cross-solver objective comparison is implied.

shots.title: Open the separate studio session
shots.chat: Switch explicitly to E5 and show the real studio request, not an invented continuation of E4.
shots.canvas: Restore the normal split workspace before entering the studio.
shots.interaction: Use the native session/branch picker; carry one continuous pointer across the transition.
shots.payoff: The film changes from exploring a batch to working with individual trials.
shots.caption: Individual trials
shots.presenterCue: A separate session asks CLIO to build an interactive studio for setting up and inspecting individual trials.

shots.title: Build and execute the recorded trials
shots.source: e5 T001/T009 jobs, semantic completion events and artifact-registration calls
shots.chat: Replay the recorded meshes, Morphorm trial, subsequent Tosca result, registration, discard and final publication in source order. Do not show the completed dashboard early.
shots.canvas: Keep chat dominant until final studio publication.
shots.interaction: Base cut uses recorded agent commands. A click on Check/Run causing new work is conditional on separately proven live routing.
shots.payoff: Recorded execution connects the configuration work to the resulting artifacts.
shots.caption: Run and inspect
shots.presenterCue: CLIO tests both solvers in short Slurm trials, checks the jobs, and registers the completed results for inspection.

shots.title: Inspect the completed studio
shots.source: e5.dashboard Geometry & Mesh and Setup tabs
shots.chat: The recorded execution is complete; the source clock is frozen.
shots.canvas: Open native Geometry & Mesh, expand the canvas, then activate Setup at 265 seconds.
shots.interaction: Inspect the real quality and boundary views, then the settings matching T001: volume fraction 0.15, filter radius 0.15, ten iterations.
shots.payoff: The controls are tied to a concrete engineering configuration.
shots.caption: Configure a trial
shots.presenterCue: The studio exposes the real solver settings and mesh information. For the recorded Morphorm test, use volume fraction 0.15, radius 0.15 and ten iterations.

shots.title: Show genuine optimization history
shots.chat: Open the result only after the recorded work and publication. Freeze source execution while inspecting its completed history.
shots.canvas: Give the Morphorm viewport useful native canvas space. Hold the camera and colour range steady during frame changes.
shots.interaction: Open the completed design at iteration ten, lower the density threshold to 0.10, replay actual frames 0–10, then restore 0.50. No invented iteration slider.
shots.payoff: The structure changes through genuine stored optimization steps.
shots.caption: Inspect the iteration history
shots.presenterCue: The completed Morphorm test includes eleven saved states, from the initial density through iteration ten. We can inspect how the material distribution changed.

shots.title: Inspect a solver field
shots.source: e5.toscaResult S_MISES and U_MAG, final cycle
shots.chat: Keep the completed source state fixed while the researcher inspects the result.
shots.canvas: Use the native Tosca field viewport with its trial identity and scale. Keep mesh and convergence context readable.
shots.interaction: Probe two actual stress values, orbit the mesh, then inspect the recorded first and last convergence points.
shots.payoff: The result can be interrogated beyond its outline.
shots.caption: Inspect the solver output
shots.presenterCue: The Tosca result includes stress and displacement fields. The Morphorm deck here supplies displacement and density, but no stress. The two test objectives use different meshes and scales.

shots.title: Keep the useful result and its record
shots.source: e5 Saved trials table and recorded lifecycle results
shots.chat: Show the relevant final public result with its source qualifications.
shots.canvas: Show the saved T001 entry and return to its result. Keep T009's discarded state accurate.
shots.interaction: Open Saved trials. No staged Save/Discard press until its live route is demonstrated.
shots.payoff: The work leaves an inspectable result and a trial record.
shots.caption: Keep the result and its context
shots.presenterCue: T001 was saved and T009 was discarded. The record preserves those decisions and the settings behind the results.

shots.title: Finish on the saved design
shots.source: e5 completed studio and T001 result
shots.chat: The completed source clock stays paused while the researcher returns to the saved design.
shots.canvas: Keep Results expanded so the final design, legend and convergence curve fit completely.
shots.interaction: Click the native Results tab, make one short orbit of T001, and hold the inspectable result.
shots.payoff: An engineering request has become work, results and a workspace the researcher can inspect.
shots.caption: Explore with CLIO
shots.presenterCue: The researcher can follow the work, compare the designs and inspect the result.

motionContract: Use editable native React components and the captured mesh/table data. Screenshots are planning references, not the film implementation.
Chat remains center-left; the native canvas carries useful inspections. Keep the workspace sidebar out of the film unless a real navigation requires it.
Use one monotonic source clock within each session and share it with visible task/artifact states. E4 and E5 have separate origins.
A deliberate inspection freezes the entire source clock through approach, native expansion, interaction and return. Resume only after restoring context.
Retype selected public explanations as contiguous prefixes, compress idle gaps, and use the NDP measured damped viewport path. Do not reveal whole paragraphs between adjacent frames.
Short completed tool groups use brief holds and visible height collapse. Do not inherit long thinking holds from SPOTTER.
One measured pointer stays above menus and fullscreen roots. Park until a 0.35-1 second approach, including the first action. No teleport, fade reset or distant return after every click.
Use native maximize only when it enables an actual inspection. Return to the conversation; do not replace interactions with slight whole-window scales.
Prewarm fonts, mesh buffers and charts. A canvas element alone is not paint readiness: require the intended artifact, frame, scalar field, threshold and case binding.
Constrain simultaneously active WebGL viewports. The 26-view smoothed dashboard is a source collection, not the film layout.
Keep technical production notes, long provenance strips, private custody paths and unsupported feature claims out of the picture. Caption review uses a separate visible footer.
No invented flow execution graph, Science Log, live iteration feed, upload, export or remote job. Include a capability only when the source and native interaction support it.

gates.required: Original hashes retained; GLB lengths/buffer ranges and finite scalar arrays validated; required tables complete. Retest actual native mesh/case bindings in the film layout.
Reconcile the 36 E5 running records against their exact matching tool.call.completed events, preserving failures and timestamps. Do not infer success merely from output presence.
Match report/surface publication and artifact arrival boundaries. The latest saved dashboard is not proof of earlier UI states; do not leak final T009/ledger data into T001 execution.
E4 orbit, threshold and linked table selection observed. Verify both selected model frame and linked data after reflow. Test any planned scalar probe before including it.
Use the 11 real E5 DENSITY frames and existing binding; no nonexistent-slider gesture. Check iteration zero remains visible at the chosen threshold and keep E4 case frames separate from time.
The recorded 10-iteration setting is shown. The mesh-size slider whose precision differs from 1/24 is excluded from the inspection.
The source defines a unitless E=1 test. A scoped viewer adapter suppresses incorrect S_MISES and U_MAG unit labels without changing original GLB bytes or numeric field arrays.

A demonstrated inline Check/Run/Save/Discard action must reach the correct session with matching parameters and a returned result before the click-driven variant is used. Planning and the base recorded-command cut can proceed.
Encoded opening, grid expansion, native case selection and restoration reviewed. Corrected AAC padding, duplicate selection clicks and WebGL probe context leakage. Full encode review still pending.
Timed presenter script plus editable captions; provide a burned-caption review copy for the Codex player and inspect its longest cue.
Render 1080p60 once the focused proofs work. Fully decode, scan adjacent frames and review encoded playback; technical checks do not establish creative approval.

productionOrder: Lock the chosen source events, chapter boundaries and short caption/presenter copy.
Implement source lifecycle reconciliation and scoped native dashboard adapters without changing originals or unrelated previews.
Measure layout, camera poses and one pointer path. Test mesh readiness, field/frame selection and data updates.
Encode a 35-45 second conversation-to-matrix proof, including actual geometry changes and the return to chat.
Encode a 25-35 second history/field proof. Resolve missing-control presentation and unit/precision issues.
Build the complete chaptered cut, then the visible-caption review copy. Use any later TIMP Q&A to refine emphasis, not as a dependency for planning.
Derive the E4 and E5 standalone cuts from the same rendered chapters; avoid independent long 3D rerenders.
exclusions: A tour of every E1-E5 dashboard or an explanation of topology-optimization mathematics
A fake calendar-chronological E4-to-E5 handoff, an invented follow-up prompt or unseen subagent work
Treating all 12 final E4 cases as steps of one changing design
A claim that any 10/50-iteration test is a converged or production-ready design
Unqualified cross-solver performance numbers, Morphorm stress, or a Tosca filter-radius control the source says is unsupported
Showing a button as the cause of commands that were actually run by the agent through scripts
Arbitrary text selection, hover tours, universal full-screen treatment, long frozen thinking or packaging/ZIP sequences
revisionNotes: V1 was rejected for raw troubleshooting, unfinished list items, internal experiment aliases and immediate-looking Slurm completion.
Standalone v2 uses explicit source-linked display copy, the actual background-array watcher and a Later time cut. The rejected interpolated clock over stale snapshots implied false per-case runtimes.
Technical checks do not establish creative approval.
